name: Gaze Selection with Anomaly-Based Error Prevention
summary: A neural network watches the gaze around each gaze selection and cancels selections whose gaze dynamics look unlike correct ones, reducing Midas-touch errors for dwell, gaze-head alignment and nod confirmation.
howItWorks: Built for an HTC Vive Pro Eye. A temporal convolutional autoencoder is trained on the gaze angular velocity just before and after correct selections; at run time, a selection whose gaze pattern is reconstructed poorly is treated as an anomaly and blocked. It is a layer on top of an existing gaze confirmation: dwell time, aligning gaze and head direction, or a head nod. In a visual-search game with 37 participants (flying robots at 18 positions across 180°, select the one marked 'C'), the system cut incorrect selections by up to 95% for dwell and gaze-head alignment and improved performance in those conditions; effects for nodding were smaller and more variable.
advantages: Removes most wrong gaze selections without changing how users select.
limitations: Needs training data and eye tracking; benefits varied across users and were small for nod confirmation.
Can also block some intended selections.

relationships.note: Adds error prevention to dwell-based gaze selection.
Adds error prevention to gaze-head alignment confirmation.
Adds error prevention to gaze selection confirmed by a nod.
